name: Qwiic / STEMMA QT (4-pin I2C)
description: The little 4-pin JST-SH connector that carries I2C (plus power) for solderless sensor/breakout chaining. SparkFun's Qwiic and Adafruit's STEMMA QT are the same connector and pinout, so they interoperate. It's just 3.3 V I2C on a keyed, polarized connector -- boards have two so you can daisy-chain a string of sensors.

contacts.name: 3V3
contacts.description: 3.3 V supply (red wire) -- Qwiic is a 3.3 V bus

variants: Qwiic (SparkFun) and STEMMA QT (Adafruit) are cross-compatible: same JST-SH 1.0mm connector, same GND/3V3/SDA/SCL order. A Qwiic cable plugs into a STEMMA QT board and vice versa.
Adafruit STEMMA (no QT, the larger JST-PH 3-pin/4-pin) is a DIFFERENT connector -- STEMMA QT is the small one that matches Qwiic.
gotchas: It's a 3.3 V bus. Powering a Qwiic chain from 5 V (or mixing a 5 V I2C device) risks the sensors -- everything on the chain shares that 3.3 V rail and the SDA/SCL levels.
Daisy-chaining is just paralleling the I2C bus, so every device on the chain needs a UNIQUE I2C address. Two of the same sensor collide unless one has an address-select jumper.
Pull-ups: each Qwiic board usually includes SDA/SCL pull-ups. A long chain of many boards stacks the pull-ups low, which can weaken the bus -- cut the pull-up jumpers on all but one if it gets flaky.
It's keyed and polarized, so you can't insert it backwards -- but the tiny latch is fragile.
notes: Qwiic / STEMMA QT 4-pin JST-SH pinout (GND/3V3/SDA/SCL). SparkFun and Adafruit variants are cross-compatible; 3.3V I2C.
